description: A path stage keeps the steps of an explanation through which a named fact reaches the value, in the order why lists them
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
shipping = 5
subtotal = price * qty
total = subtotal + shipping
(total |> why |> path(price)).map(step -> step.node)

description: After affects, a path stage keeps what a change moves on its way to the target and leaves out what it moves elsewhere
code:
price = 10
tax = price * 2
net = price + 1
total = tax + net
label = total * 3
report = price - 1
(price |> affects |> path(total)).map(step -> step.node)

description: Every path through a diamond is kept in walk order, and a value that does not reach the target is dropped
code:
seed = 2
left = seed + 1
right = seed * 3
spare = 7
joined = left + right + spare
(joined |> why |> path(seed)).map(step -> step.node)

description: A path selection is empty while no path reaches the target and fills in when a rule is rewired to read it
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
z = 9
gap = b |> why |> path(z)
before = suppose: gap.length
a = z + 1
[before, gap.map(step -> step.node)]

description: A class-level rule gives each instance its own path from its total to its price
code:
class Item(price, qty):
    this.price = price
    this.qty = qty
$Item.total = $Item.price * $Item.qty + 1
$Item.via = $Item.total |> why |> path($Item.price)
pen = Item(2, 5)
cup = Item(3, 1)
[pen.via.map(step -> step.node), cup.via.map(step -> step.holds)]

description: A path stage composes with the state filters in either order, so the derived steps of a path and the stated facts on it can be asked for directly
code:
base = 2
rate = base * 2
fee = 1
cost = rate * 4 + fee
[(cost |> why |> path(base) |> derived).map(step -> step.node), (cost |> why |> stated |> path(base)).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A reference or the model without a walk uses the direction of why, so the model path of a fact is the fact and everything that rests on it
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
subtotal = price * qty
other = qty + 1
[(model |> path(price)).map(step -> step.node), (subtotal |> path(price)).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A function named path shadows the stage, which then raises a TypeError, while the function itself keeps working
code:
price = 10
total = price * 2
def path(x) => x + 1
try:
    total |> why |> path(price)
catch error:
    failure = error
[path(1), failure]
